frases: A bug showed up in one of the last {show mil}thousand commits.
Are you going to test them one by [-one]?
No need: {show bis}git bisect finds it with a [+binary] search.
{show c}First you start, {type c}mark the current commit as bad and an old one as good.
Now Git knows between which two points to [+search].
Git puts you on the {show p1}middle commit, and {good p1}you test it.
You mark it {show p2}good or bad based on the {good p2}result.
So {show p3}half of what is left is {good p3}[+ruled] out.
Since each test cuts the rest in half, a thousand commits take about {show n}{boom n +0.4}[+ten] tests.
At the end, {show rs}git bisect reset takes you back to where you were.
If they ask you, [+say]: git bisect {show fl1}splits the history in half {show fl2}until it finds the guilty commit.
lineas: git bisect: binary search in the history
